blockers: codex has required edits: Amend the closure-authentication design so every fs-verity-measured closure member and verdict-affecting runtime input is bound by inode—not subsequently resolved through a mutable staging pathname. For example, retain an fd for the measured inode and individually attach that exact inode into the private mount namespace using a file bind mount or open_tree/move_mount equivalent, then freeze the root’s complete directory membership. Add rename/unlink-and-replace-after-verification regressions for ld.so, a DT_NEEDED library, git/credential helpers, and CA inputs; the replacement inode must never be executed or read. Clarify the distinct ordinary-content and fs-verity digest pins, then re-freeze and re-authorize the resulting plan hash.

codex has hard stops: The asserted mutation-point binding for the authenticated dynamic/exec closure is incomplete: fs-verity protects an inode’s contents but explicitly still permits rename, deletion, and linking. A concurrent same-user writer can rename or unlink a verified verity file in the plain staging directory and replace its pathname with an unauthenticated inode before ld.so, a helper, or the trust-store consumer opens it. The existing overwrite regressions do not exercise this pathname-rebinding attack, so the plan does not presently prove that the bytes read or executed are the bytes authenticated.
